what_happened: An operator edited the config by hand and set [parallel] max_concurrency back to 1. The earlier setting was 2. The first run with two jobs at once had two of three jobs hit their deadlines because local builds contended for the machine. Rust jobs still build locally after routing (#126). No job was rejected by a reviewer in this event. The operator rolled back a tuning step on purpose.
cause: Athena treats the parallelism limit as a fixed number that an operator picks. It does not measure what the local machine can bear, which includes CPU and build contention as well as disk, and it does not enforce a limit. Build work runs on the same machine as the queue, so concurrent jobs compete for it. Deadlines are fixed, so contention shows up as timeouts, not as a signal that the setting is too high. The operator found the safe value only by trying it, and rolled back after jobs failed.
prevention: Make the drain choose and enforce concurrency from measured local capacity, instead of a hand-set number. Count local-build jobs (such as Rust) against a separate, lower limit, with a default of 1 while builds run on this machine. Check free disk and load before starting another job. If a job exceeds its deadline while running alongside others, lower the limit automatically and record why. Raise the limit only when builds run off this machine.
proposed_request: Make the queue drain's parallelism safe on a machine that builds locally. Outcome: running plan groups two at a time must not cause deadline failures from build contention. Before starting another concurrent job, the drain should check local capacity (free disk and CPU load) and count jobs that build locally (such as Rust) against a separate limit that defaults to 1 while builds run on this machine. If a job hits its deadline while others run alongside it, the drain should lower its concurrency, log the reason, and not count the timeout as a real failure of the work. The configured max_concurrency should act as an upper bound, not the value actually used. Show this with a test where two local-build jobs are queued with max_concurrency set to 2 and only one runs at a time, and a test where two non-build jobs do run together.
